info.title: Giano Wallet API
info.description: WebAuthn ceremonies, sessions and policied ERC-4337 user-operation relay for Giano smart wallets (multi-tenant, multi-chain).

session.description: Opaque session token from a ceremony verify endpoint

adminKey.description: Per-tenant admin API key, issued by an admin

platformSession.description: Platform admin session from POST /v1/platform/auth/verify (EIP-4361 sign-in)

post.summary: Revoke the live sessions of one of this tenant's users, by externalUserId or wallet address (G5)

put.summary: Replace this tenant's sponsorship rules (for one chain)
put.description: Full replace, validated on write. Rejected with per-path messages on any violation, so an invalid rule set is never stored and therefore never interpreted permissively. Rules are per chain and never inherited from another chain (MC-67): enabling a new chain is an explicit act.

patch.summary: Update fields of this tenant's sponsorship rules (for one chain)
patch.description: Shallow field-level merge over the stored configuration, then validated as a whole — so a partial update cannot leave the rule set in a state a full replace would have rejected.

get.summary: Who changed the sponsorship rules, and when
This tenant's gas balance, reservations and where to fund
get.description: Read live from the paymaster contract, with the block it was read at, so the figures can be reproduced from the chain rather than taken on trust.

get.summary: What this tenant has been charged, broken down
get.description: One row per settled operation, with gas, Giano's fee and the overhead allowance kept separate — each row traceable to a `Sponsored` event on chain.

get.summary: Every sponsorship decision, allowed or refused, with the rule-by-rule results
get.description: Includes the pre-approval checks that never became transactions — those are exactly the decisions a user was shown, so they are what answers "why did my user see a refusal?".

get.summary: This tenant's transaction display mappings for one chain
Who changed the transaction display mappings, and when

put.summary: Create or replace the mapping for a contract (for one chain)
put.description: The body is an ERC-7730 descriptor with an inline ABI. Validated on write with one issue per violation, each with its JSON path; nothing is stored unless every check passes. The descriptor must bind the requested chain and contract in context.contract.deployments. Bodies over 64 KiB are refused.

delete.summary: Remove the mapping for a contract (for one chain)

get.summary: The tenant's transaction display mappings for one chain, as the wallet consumes them
get.description: ERC-7730 descriptors, re-validated on read: a stored descriptor that no longer passes validation is omitted (and flagged on the admin listing) rather than served. The tenant is the Origin header when present, else the Host (a same-origin GET carries no Origin). Cached for a minute by the wallet.

post.description: Decides whether to sponsor a user operation for the session's tenant, and if so issues an authorisation the paymaster contract verifies on-chain. Refusals carry a stable machine-readable reason in `error.data.reason`.

post.summary: Sign out everywhere: revokes every live session of the calling user, this one included

post.description: The bundler surface a wallet origin points its bundler client at, so the bundler itself never has to be reachable from a browser. eth_sendUserOperation goes through the same policy, audit and idempotency pipeline as POST /v1/userops; eth_estimateUserOperationGas is bound to the session wallet; eth_getUserOperationReceipt and eth_getUserOperationByHash are forwarded; eth_chainId and eth_supportedEntryPoints are answered from configuration. Refusals carry a stable code in `error.code`.

Refusals carry a stable code in `error.code`.

Forwards read-only JSON-RPC methods to the chain node wallet-api is configured with, so a wallet origin needs no RPC URL of its own and a keyed provider URL never reaches a browser. Tenant-bound by Origin, rate-limited per tenant; eth_chainId is answered from configuration; anything outside the read allowlist is refused with -32601.

post.summary: Chain RPC read relay for platform admins (JSON-RPC)
post.description: What the paymaster console reads the chain through. Forwards the same read-only JSON-RPC methods as /v1/rpc, for a platform admin session only. eth_getLogs must name a blockHash or a hex range of at most 10000 blocks (-32602 otherwise); 1200 forwarded reads per session per minute (-32021 beyond); bodies over 16384 bytes are refused with 413.

Sponsorship decisions and settlements on one chain, in total and per tenant; the last 7 days unless given, at most 90
The status of every served chain, probed in parallel with a 3-second timeout each; never a node or bundler URL
